what_this_is: a committed watchlist of taxa a public-health reader would want asked about in a wastewater library. It is a SCREENING PANEL, not a ranking: every entry is reported whether or not it was seen, because a taxon looked for and not found is a result and an empty row is not.
how_a_row_is_counted: pairs under the whole clade of the taxid, not the exact taxid. A read Kraken2 places at `Enterovirus C` and one it places at a serotype beneath it are the same answer to a reader, and requiring an exact match would report absence for a taxon the classifier placed one rank up.
what_a_detection_is_not: a species call from a 107 nt read against a k-mer index is a claim about shared k-mers with a reference. It is not a diagnosis, not a viable organism, and not a case. Every row is reported at three confidence thresholds because the classified fraction moves by an order of magnitude across them.
what_an_absence_is_not: evidence that the organism is not in the catchment. This is an untargeted shotgun library, which the literature reports as insensitive for human pathogens at wastewater concentrations; the bound each absent row carries is a bound on what this sequencing could have seen.
selection: chosen for what a public-health reader asks of sewage: the enteric viruses wastewater surveillance was built on, the respiratory and vaccine-preventable viruses it was extended to, the notifiable bacterial enteric pathogens, the ESKAPE organisms that carry antimicrobial resistance, and the waterborne parasites. Not chosen by looking at this sample, which would make every row a foregone conclusion.
taxonomy: taxids are the scientific names in data/k2_pluspf08/names.dmp, resolved against that file

entries.name: Norovirus
entries.why: the commonest cause of epidemic gastroenteritis and the most-watched target in wastewater

entries.name: Rotavirus A
entries.why: the leading cause of severe childhood diarrhoea and a vaccine-programme indicator

entries.name: Hepatovirus A
entries.why: hepatitis A, faecal-oral, outbreak-prone in low-vaccination groups

entries.name: Hepatitis E virus
entries.why: waterborne hepatitis, zoonotic in Europe via pigs

entries.name: Enterovirus
entries.why: includes poliovirus, EV-D68 and EV-A71; the genus polio surveillance watches

entries.name: Enterovirus C
entries.why: the species containing the polioviruses, reported separately from the genus

entries.name: Sapovirus
entries.why: gastroenteritis, under-ascertained clinically and visible in sewage

entries.name: Mamastrovirus
entries.why: human astroviruses, paediatric gastroenteritis

entries.name: Mastadenovirus
entries.why: enteric adenovirus types 40/41, and a classic faecal indicator

entries.name: Kobuvirus
entries.why: Aichivirus A, gastroenteritis, routinely abundant in sewage

entries.name: Parechovirus
entries.why: neonatal sepsis and meningitis; shed in faeces

entries.name: Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2
entries.why: the virus that made wastewater surveillance routine

entries.name: Influenza A virus
entries.why: seasonal and pandemic influenza, including avian spillover

entries.name: Influenza B virus
entries.why: seasonal influenza

entries.name: Orthopneumovirus
entries.why: respiratory syncytial virus, a major infant hospitalisation cause

entries.name: Measles morbillivirus
entries.why: outbreaks follow vaccination gaps and wastewater detection precedes case reports

entries.name: Mumps orthorubulavirus
entries.why: vaccine-preventable, shed in urine and saliva

entries.name: Rubella virus
entries.why: congenital rubella is the reason elimination is tracked

entries.name: Orthopoxvirus
entries.why: the genus containing mpox and smallpox

entries.name: Human immunodeficiency virus 1
entries.why: bloodborne; a detection in sewage would be unexpected and worth explaining

entries.name: Hepatitis B virus
entries.why: bloodborne hepatitis

entries.name: Dengue virus
entries.why: arboviral, imported-case indicator

entries.name: West Nile virus
entries.why: arboviral, bird reservoir, local transmission in Europe

entries.name: Salmonella enterica
entries.why: salmonellosis, notifiable in most countries

entries.name: Shigella
entries.why: shigellosis, low infectious dose, faecal-oral

entries.name: Vibrio cholerae
entries.why: cholera; the organism wastewater surveillance was invented for

entries.name: Campylobacter jejuni
entries.why: the commonest bacterial gastroenteritis in Europe

entries.name: Yersinia enterocolitica
entries.why: foodborne gastroenteritis

entries.name: Listeria monocytogenes
entries.why: foodborne, high case fatality in pregnancy and the elderly

entries.name: Clostridioides difficile
entries.why: healthcare-associated diarrhoea, spore-forming, survives treatment

entries.name: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
entries.why: tuberculosis; wastewater detection is an active research question

entries.name: Legionella pneumophila
entries.why: legionellosis; an environmental organism with a water route

entries.name: Leptospira
entries.why: leptospirosis, rodent urine, flood-associated

entries.name: Helicobacter pylori
entries.why: gastric cancer risk; a possible waterborne route

entries.name: Escherichia coli
entries.why: mostly commensal here: it is the faecal indicator organism, not by itself a pathogen signal

entries.name: Klebsiella pneumoniae
entries.why: ESKAPE; carbapenem resistance spreads through sewage

entries.name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
entries.why: ESKAPE; environmental reservoir and hospital pathogen

entries.name: Staphylococcus aureus
entries.why: ESKAPE; MRSA community carriage

entries.name: Enterococcus faecium
entries.why: ESKAPE; vancomycin resistance, and a faecal indicator

entries.name: Acinetobacter baumannii
entries.why: ESKAPE; highly drug-resistant hospital pathogen

entries.name: Cryptosporidium
entries.why: chlorine-tolerant, drinking-water outbreaks

entries.name: Giardia
entries.why: giardiasis, cyst-forming, waterborne

entries.name: Entamoeba histolytica
entries.why: amoebic dysentery, faecal-oral

entries.name: Toxoplasma gondii
entries.why: oocysts shed by cats reach water
